articles.title: Pope Leo welcomed by millions in his second ‘homeland’ of Peru
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV has been welcomed by a few million people upon his arrival in Peru, his adopted homeland, for the final leg of a three-nation Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for ...
articles.body_text:
Pope Leo XIV has been welcomed by a few million people upon his arrival in Peru, his adopted homeland, for the final leg of a three-nation Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

People waving flags and wearing pope-themed shirts filled the main plaza in Lima and erupted into loud cheers as a big screen showed the plane touching down on Wednesday local time. Some held signs that read, “Welcome home”.

A Vatican statement said three million people greeted the pontiff in Lima, setting another record for the biggest crowd of his papacy after an estimated 2.5 million people attended an outdoor Mass in Buenos Aires earlier this week.

The 71-year-old travelled to Uruguay and Argentina before heading to Peru.

The pope was born in Chicago, the United States, but served in Peru as a missionary priest and bishop for two decades and obtained citizenship there, before being tapped to lead the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.

The pontiff said his return to Peru held “a very special meaning”.

“Today, I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you,” he said at Lima’s Gran Teatro Nacional. “I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am returning to my homeland.”

Peru prepared for the homecoming by erecting a 14-metre (46ft) statue of Pope Leo with outstretched arms, towering over a seaside park in Callao. Merchants in Lima were selling pope-themed shirts and souvenirs.

The pontiff is scheduled to spend three days in the northern city of Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023.

In a closely watched speech to President Keiko Fujimori, whose father Alberto Fujimori led Peru through the turbulent 1990s and a brutal war against Maoist Shining Path rebels, Pope Leo urged the president to build confidence among her people after her narrow election victory earlier this year.

He invited Fujimori to confront the wounds of the country’s turbulent past, alluding to her father’s contested legacy. “Past events deserve to be treated with justice and sensitivity, leaving room for harmony to grow ‌and for differences ⁠to be addressed with respect,” he said.

The pontiff also called on Peruvians to cultivate “honesty, integrity, and a willingness to engage with others”, saying those qualities were essential to sustaining trust and democratic institutions.

In welcoming the pope, Fujimori said his visit was an invitation for Peru to pursue its “unfinished task” of national reconciliation.

When Alberto Fujimori was pardoned in 2017, Leo – then Bishop Robert Prevost – criticised the move, saying the former president should personally seek forgiveness from victims if Peru were to achieve genuine reconciliation.

Pope Leo began the trip less than a month after lung cancer surgery and has appeared in good form, making long speeches in a firm, clear voice.

articles.title: Fewer hours and higher wages – or more burnout and surveillance: employers told to prepare for AI
articles.excerpt:
Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launches best practice guide on AI adoption after Qantas and Canva job cuts

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Entry-level jo...
articles.body_text:
Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launches best practice guide on AI adoption after Qantas and Canva job cuts

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Entry-level jobs will be the first to be automated due to AI, but it could mean fewer hours and higher wages for ordinary workers – or make jobs tougher with more burnout and workplace surveillance – the government has warned employers.

While major companies like Qantas and Canva slash their workforces in restructures spurred by AI changes, workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth said employers must give workers “a clear plan” about how automation could affect their jobs, and the opportunity to move into new roles.

As she launched a new government guide on AI and employment – which cautioned that younger, older and First Nations workers, along with women and people with a disability faced “disproportionate impacts” – another Labor MP, Ed Husic, questioned what workers will get from the AI revolution.

“Who receives the benefits of higher productivity?” Husic, the former industry minister, told a parliamentary hearing examining the big four banks.

“Does it mean better services and lower prices for customers, secure jobs with higher wages for workers, or just lower labour costs and higher returns?”

Rishworth on Thursday launched a “best practice guide on the adoption of AI in the workplace”, saying the new technology must benefit both businesses and employees.

The guide paints an optimistic picture of AI, saying wider takeup could improve productivity, service quality and profitability for businesses, as well as boost wages, offer shorter and more flexible working hours, or provide more meaningful work for employees.

But deeper within the document, it also concedes there are “potential hazards” of AI, including “intrusive worker surveillance, poor rostering practices, intensified or unrealistic performance standards” and potential discrimination.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

It suggests that, if basic tasks are automated, humans will be left with more intense and complex tasks – and that some employers could use greater monitoring capabilities for performance management.

In a speech to a business forum in Sydney, Rishworth said some firms had used AI to automate tedious tasks to save time and money, but warned that firms simply adding AI to their company without properly consulting workers could actually increase workloads, as humans have to navigate an added step.

“I’ve spoken to many workers who have told me that they are willing to adopt AI at work where they can see that it will improve their working life. But that willingness cannot be taken for granted,” Rishworth said.

“Will they receive support and opportunities to build new skills? Will their knowledge and expertise still be valued? Will they share in the benefits being created? Without answers to these questions, workers will naturally lose trust in the process and become reluctant to engage with new technologies,” she said.

Greens leader David Shoebridge accused the government of “watching from the sidelines” while big companies slashed their workforce, demanding protection against surveillance and job cuts.

“When the government talks about asking employers nicely to consult staff, what it is really saying is that a worker who loses their job to an algorithm will have no legal recourse at all.

“We have seen Qantas, Canva, NAB and ANZ all firing Australian workers as part of offshoring and an AI rollout – it’s clear the time for optional guidelines has passed,” he said.

“Sharing the benefits of AI through better pay and shorter hours is a good idea, and it is exactly why it needs to be written into law instead of left to the goodwill of employers.”

The Reserve Bank this week reported it had seen “little evidence to date” of AI disrupting Australia’s labour market, but said the size and type of future impacts were “highly uncertain”.

The RBA – which last week warned the construction of datacentres and AI investment was fuelling inflation – said it saw “tentative signs” of impacts on certain roles, like clerks, computer programmers and call centre workers.

Qantas this week announced 850 job cuts which would target finance, human resources and marketing roles. Meanwhile, National Australian Bank announced 2,500 job losses and while Canva announced 1,200 layoffs.

All have been linked partly to the growth in AI.

Rishworth’s workplace guide says little about potential redundancies linked to AI, but warns employers they should be consulting with workers about the takeup of AI and what it might mean for their jobs. It especially raises concern about “entry-level work”, which the guide said may be “the first to be automated”.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s legacy: Personality politics reshapes Israeli democracy
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a national unity government – at least among Jewish Israelis – during the swearing-in of Israel’s new parliament, or Knesset, on Tuesday, hoping to cling t...
articles.body_text:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a national unity government – at least among Jewish Israelis – during the swearing-in of Israel’s new parliament, or Knesset, on Tuesday, hoping to cling to power. The opposition to him, which now has a majority of seats but has yet to form a government, reacted with heckles, catcalls, and walkouts.

Citing supposed internal and external threats, Netanyahu called for unity with the opposition bloc that has been tasked with forming a government to replace him. Netanyahu pointed to the threat posed by Iran and the increased number of democratically elected lawmakers who are Palestinian citizens of Israel, whom he accused, without evidence, of seeking Israel’s destruction.

“We must do one thing – set aside every other consideration and form a national unity government. Only such a government will be able to meet challenges of this magnitude. It is impossible to handle them with a narrow government,” he said of the potential for a minority government that many analysts consider likely after coalition negotiations are complete.

“I say this because here in this parliament they are seriously talking about forming a narrow government like this, a government that includes within it terror supporters, haters of Israel, or that would be dependent on them,” he said, referring to the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Even by the standards of Israeli politics, where analysts say personality has long overshadowed party and policy, Tuesday’s session was unusually contentious.

Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett heckled Netanyahu while trading barbs with the latter’s wife, Sara, and his hard-right ally Itamar Ben-Gvir, while many of the Palestinian lawmakers attacked by the prime minister during his speech walked out in protest.

Gadi Eisenkot, who has been given the first chance to form a new government, subsequently cancelled previously scheduled coalition talks with Netanyahu and declared him “unfit for office”.

Netanyahu has long played an outsized role in Israeli politics, helping transform the political system into one that is highly based on personalities, with voters typically identifying a leader they like first, and then focusing on policy discussions. Nevertheless, despite having contributed more to that change than any other politician, Netanyahu now finds himself fighting for his political life.

If Eisenkot is able to form a viable new government – which still hangs in the balance – Netanyahu faces being frozen out of power, and a future in which his corruption trial continues without the protection of the prime minister’s office. There will also likely be an inquiry into his and his government’s failings in the run-up to the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023.

His potential downfall, however, does not mean an end to personality politics in Israel. Instead, it may be one of the most lasting parts of his legacy, said Roi Zur, an Israeli specialist in voting behaviour and election strategies at the University of Essex.

“Netanyahu Americanised the party system in Israel and made Likud a populist party,” he said of the influences the country’s longest-serving prime minister has had on Israel and his own party.

“It is a clear case in Israel that the person at the head of the list or the head of the party is very important, and politics evolve around the head of the party,” Zur said. “We see it in how people think about political parties or voting in general in Israel. When you ask people, ‘Who are you voting for?’, they say, ‘I vote for Netanyahu, I vote for Bennett, I vote for Eisenkot,’ whilst in the past it was ‘I vote for Likud, I vote for Labor,’ and so on.”

Dahlia Schneidlin, an American-Israeli pollster, noted that Israeli political campaigns had become more personalised in the past few decades even though elections in the country are almost all based on voting for a party slate, and not individuals.

That had led to many cases where voters focus on the personality rather than the party, and vote accordingly.

However, the Israeli electoral system almost always leads to coalition governments. And bringing other parties into a coalition often needs leaders to demonstrate “political neogitiating and bargaining skills”, Schneidlin said, as they try to encourage others to join them.

Eisenkot, Schneidlin said, will have to demonstrate those skills if he is to form a government, rather than simply being focused on his own personality.

But the emphasis on differences in political personality over policy positions has fuelled a culture where personal differences, such as those between Netanyahu and opposition stalwart Avigdor Lieberman – whose shared animosity is well known but whose right-wing political positions are in some ways very close – contribute to a populist politics easily understood by a public eager to see itself as politically engaged.

“The stress on the personal makes everything so much worse,” Yossi Mekelberg, a senior fellow at Chatham House, said. “With party structures so centralised, leaders can become almost dictatorial and get to act without constraint. This is how it becomes possible for a prime minister to accuse 19 elected members of the Knesset of being terrorist sympathisers and nobody thinks it’s extraordinary. It’s become toxic,” he said.

articles.title: Israeli strikes hit medical complex as nine killed across Gaza
articles.excerpt: Israeli attacks have killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heav...
articles.body_text:
Israeli attacks have killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heavy rains.

At least four Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza in the early hours of Thursday, according to Gaza’s Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal.

An Israeli air attack on Wednesday killed 38-year-old Mohammed Salem al-Daash in the al-Sabra neighbourhood, south of Gaza City.

Another Palestinian was shot and killed by Israeli forces east of the al-Bureij camp in central Gaza, and another was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the al-Nasr neighbourhood, northwest of Gaza City.

At least two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in a strike targeting a tent sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood, north of Gaza City.

Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary, reporting from Gaza City, described the Israeli attacks as indiscriminate targeting of civilians, saying people who were carrying on with simple attempts to survive lost their lives, such as “a man filling up a water tank, [who] was killed in a drone strike”.

“In another attack, two brothers from the al-Absi family were killed while they were sheltering inside their tent on al-Jalaa Street,” she said, adding that nowhere in Gaza was safe.

The Israeli attacks came as the UN appealed for more tents to be sent to the enclave because at least 70,000 tents were flooded in weekend rains, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

Heavy rain has directly affected at least 106,000 people in Gaza in recent days, according to UNICEF, with thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians submerged under water and latrines overflowing into camps.

NGOs and local organisations say they do not have the resources or capacity to deal with the crisis, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of essential aid.

“Ultimately, we need the Israeli authorities to cooperate with giving the permissions so that we can bring those tents in,” UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq told reporters at a media briefing, adding that apart from funding, Israeli permits were needed “to get this in”.

Certain countries supporting aid deliveries to Gaza say that delivering winter supplies will have to wait for the formation of an Israeli government, said Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs.

In a statement, Fletcher said foreign ministers have assured their support, “but also repeatedly said that progress would be hard until after Israeli elections. Now we’re told to wait for the formation of a government”.

“This is not an acceptable excuse,” he added, citing international law and the consequences of delays, blockages and funding cuts.

Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Wednesday that Rome has launched a new emergency initiative worth 5 million euros ($5.5m) to provide immediate assistance to the Gaza Strip following the flooding.

The death toll from the Israeli genocidal war in Gaza has surged to 74,653 civilians killed since October 7, 2023, medical sources told the Palestinian Wafa news agency on Wednesday.

An additional 176,007 Palestinians have been injured in the past three years.

Israel has killed 1,622 Palestinians and injured 5,878 others since the Gaza “ceasefire” agreement came into effect on October 11, 2025.

articles.title: Iran escalates in Hormuz, claims strike on Omani island it says 'enemy' uses for US military ops
articles.excerpt:
The IRGC reported a strike against ‘enemy navigation aid systems,’ radar and communications equipment located on Didamar Island in Hormuz (Credit: Reuters).

Iran claims it struck a small Omani island...
articles.body_text:
The IRGC reported a strike against ‘enemy navigation aid systems,’ radar and communications equipment located on Didamar Island in Hormuz (Credit: Reuters).

Iran claims it struck a small Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting oil tanker navigation infrastructure as CENTCOM maintains its blockade of Iranian ports and protects commercial shipping from Iranian attacks along the southern route.

Three sources also confirmed to Reuters Wednesday that navigation systems and communications equipment on Didamar Island, also known as Little Quoin Island, had been attacked, raising concerns about the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure used to maintain oil shipments through the Gulf.

Iran's semiofficial Fars News Agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy targeted the island, alleging the systems were being used to help vessels transit the strait without Tehran's authorization.

WHITE HOUSE SILENT ON IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ PLAN TEHRAN SAYS WOULD BAN US WARSHIPS

A satellite image shows Didamar Island, Oman (Google/Airbus/Handout via Reuters)

Iranian state television also claimed that personnel and equipment on the island "were helping the flow of oil smuggling by the enemy," with the IRGC maintaining it had carried out the strikes, Reuters reported.

Video published by Reuters showed smoke rising near the rocky outcrop.

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said it identified the attack as occurring Nov. 8, before Iranian state media claimed responsibility on Nov. 10.

ISW also questioned the extent of the reported damage, noting that commercial vessels continued using the southern route after the attack.

"The extent of the damage to these systems and the systems struck remains unclear at the time of this writing," ISW said in its assessment.

Satellite imagery from the European Union's Copernicus Sentinel-2 program, cited by Reuters and dated Nov. 8, also showed apparent scorch marks near radar and radio equipment on the island.

TRADE VESSEL STRUCK BY PROJECTILE IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AMID US-IRAN TALKS

A ship passes through the Strait of Hormuz during a two-week temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran April 8, 2026. (Shady Alassar/Anadolu/Getty Images)

The strike comes as U.S. forces carry out missions to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

The U.S. Navy imposed its blockade of Iranian ports in April after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in February amid escalating tensions. The U.S. lifted the blockade in June following a temporary ceasefire agreement, but then reinstated it in July.

Commercial and allied shipping through the waterway is advised to use a southern route through Omani territorial waters, located outside of Tehran’s direct military control and overseen by CENTCOM.

The latest incident on Didamar Island comes as Gulf oil exporters work to restore shipments disrupted by the conflict.

TRUMP MEETS KEY IRAN WAR MEDIATOR AS UAE REVEALS MAJOR OIL EXPORT SURGE DESPITE CONFLICT

An Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps speedboat sails in the Persian Gulf during an IRGC marine parade marking Persian Gulf National Day near the Bushehr nuclear power plant in Bushehr, Iran, April 29, 2024. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

According to Reuters, regional oil exports recovered to more than 80% of prewar levels in September and October, aided by CENTCOM and increased Saudi exports through the Red Sea.

Shipping companies have also relied on offshore tanker-to-tanker transfers near Oman and the United Arab Emirates to maintain flows.

Didamar, meanwhile, belongs to Oman, making the reported attack particularly sensitive as Tehran seeks to disrupt maritime operations in the region. It is a small, uninhabited rocky island roughly 10 nautical miles north of the tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula, near one of the principal commercial shipping routes through the strait.

The island has long served as a navigational landmark for vessels traveling along the waterway, including through a lighthouse established in 1914.

Its maritime infrastructure reportedly includes a radar system mounted on a roughly 25-meter tower and radio communications equipment used to assist vessels navigating the narrow passage.

The island has also been associated with the Hormuz Control Centre, which coordinates maritime traffic in the area.

OIL SQUEEZE TIGHTENS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS CRIPPLE HORMUZ ESCAPE ROUTES

A satellite image shows the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime passage connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, vital for global energy supply. (Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)

Arabian Maritime and Navigation Aids Services (AMMAS) has been identified as a provider of navigational support infrastructure in the region, including maritime lights, buoys and other equipment.

The reported Didamar attack also follows U.S. military operations against Iranian targets elsewhere in the waterway.

U.S. forces struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island Nov. 2, and officials described the strikes as "defensive" actions targeting Iranian surface-to-air missile threats.

Qeshm Island, located near the Strait of Hormuz, is home to Iranian naval facilities and military infrastructure associated with the Revolutionary Guard.

President Donald Trump also acknowledged Nov. 6 that American forces continue to conduct limited strikes against Iranian targets.

Asked by a reporter about the strikes near Qeshm Island, Trump said, "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title: Tunnel to Towers pays off mortgages for 30 military families in Veterans Day tribute: 'A great sacrifice'
articles.excerpt: Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller announces plans to pay off 30 mortgages for families of fallen service members. He also discusses housing programs for homeless veterans, a new facility in Harrisburg...
articles.body_text:
Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller announces plans to pay off 30 mortgages for families of fallen service members. He also discusses housing programs for homeless veterans, a new facility in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania and the foundation's goal of delivering 343 mortgage-free homes in honor of the 9/11 victims.

The Tunnel to Towers Foundation marked Veterans Day on Wednesday by announcing mortgage payoffs for 30 families of fallen military heroes across the country, helping ensure their loved ones have a permanent place to call home.

The families span 22 states and represent nearly every branch of the U.S. military, according to the foundation, which provides mortgage-free homes to surviving spouses and children of service members and first responders who died in the line of duty or from service-related illnesses.

Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller shared the news Wednesday on "Fox & Friends" to discuss the mortgages, as well as its housing program for homeless veterans in Pennsylvania and its upcoming "Season of Hope" initiative for firefighters' families.

"Number one is that we are paying off 30 mortgages to Gold Star families that lost their loved ones for our country. Many of them are dying of burn pit cancers, just like many of our first responders are still dying from 9/11 illnesses. It's very sad," Siller said. "So on a day like today, we want to make sure that America doesn't forget that there's a great sacrifice always being made for our country. We get to live in this great country. There are people out there that are still dying for us."

9/11 HERO’S MEMORY PRESERVED THROUGH MASSIVE EFFORT TO ‘DO GOOD’ FOR VETS, FIRST RESPONDERS: ‘HIS LEGACY’

Tunnel to Towers Foundation representatives and guests cut the ribbon at the grand opening of the Harrisburg Veterans Village in Pennsylvania on Wednesday. (Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The Veterans Day announcement is part of a larger commitment to deliver 343 mortgage-free homes in 2026, a tribute to the 343 New York City firefighters who lost their lives during the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

The milestone comes as the nation commemorates the 25th anniversary of 9/11, a tragedy that inspired the foundation's creation and its ongoing mission to support military families and first responders.

"So we made a promise this year for the 25th anniversary that we're going to deliver 343 mortgage-free homes this year, one for every firefighter who died on 9/11. That's almost a house a day," Siller said. "From Thanksgiving to the Christmas is the remainder of those homes, over 60 homes that we'll be delivering, and it hit our 343 mark for the 25th anniversary."

Among those whose families were recognized Wednesday were Army Lt. Col. David Briseno of Grand Prairie, Texas; Marine Corps Master Sgt. Khanh Tuan "Shane" Nguyen of Annapolis, Maryland; Army Sgt. Brandon Minneman of Olympia, Washington; and Navy Chief Petty Officer Ernest Lopez Jr. of Oakdale, California.

Other recipients included families in New York, Georgia, Tennessee, Illinois, Massachusetts and several more states.

Through its Gold Star Family Home Program, the foundation seeks to ease the financial burden on families coping with the loss of a loved one who served their country.

AMERICA'S WOUNDED, STRUGGLING VETERANS GET BRAND-NEW HOMES BUILT BY FLORIDA TEENS

Pennsylvania state troopers salute during a Veterans Day flag ceremony at the grand opening of the Tunnel to Towers Foundation's Harrisburg Veterans Village on Wednesday. (Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

The program provides mortgage-free homes to eligible surviving spouses with young children, offering long-term housing stability following the death of a parent.

In addition to the mortgage payoffs, Tunnel to Towers celebrated the grand opening of its Harrisburg Veterans Village in Pennsylvania on Veterans Day, expanding its efforts to combat homelessness among former service members. The new development sits on the former Phoenix Mill property, where construction began in April 2025.

The foundation transformed the waterfront site on the Susquehanna River into a residential community featuring a 61-unit apartment complex and 20 one-bedroom comfort homes. The development is designed to house more than 80 veterans in need of permanent housing while providing access to services intended to help residents rebuild their lives.

Those services include job training, assistance obtaining veterans benefits, mental health support and addiction treatment.

STEEL ACROSS AMERICA ENDS ITS CROSS-COUNTRY 9/11 MEMORIAL AT NY GIANTS GAME

Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller speaks at the grand opening of the Harrisburg Veterans Village in Pennsylvania on Veterans Day, Wednesday. (Tunnel to Towers Foundation)

"I said, 'Hey, think about somebody who's overseas protecting us, right, and the guy next to him gets blown up, and it happens over and over again. They come back here to the states, and they're not all part of the military anymore, now they have to assimilate back into society.’ A lot of them have real problems doing that, and they end up on the streets. It's not acceptable," Siller said. "A couple of years ago, we Tunnel for Towers, we made a promise we're going to eradicate homelessness amongst our veterans. In the last three years, we've taken 27,500 homeless veterans off the streets.

"We build these beautiful hotels, and then we remodel them into apartments for these permanent apartments for the older homeless veterans, and we put comfort homes on these properties. They're 500 square foot houses, and they have their own homes."

The foundation said its approach goes beyond providing shelter by addressing the emotional, financial and medical challenges that can contribute to homelessness among veterans.

The Tunnels to Towers Foundation honors firefighters and first responders during its annual 5K Run and Walk NYC event. (Tunnels to Towers)

Tunnel to Towers launched its Homeless Veteran Program in 2022, with the goal of ensuring that veterans who served their country do not have to live on its streets.

Since the program began, the organization says it has provided housing assistance and supportive services to more than 20,000 veterans and 10,000 children.

The Harrisburg location joins Veterans Villages already operating in Memphis, Tennessee; North Charleston, South Carolina; Houston, Texas; and Atlanta, Georgia.

The foundation also supports affiliated veteran housing programs in Riverside and West Los Angeles, California, and Austin, Texas.

Another Veterans Village is scheduled to open Dec. 9 in Denver, Colorado, while seven additional developments are under construction and expected to open in 2027.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

articles.title: Bengals coach Zac Taylor acknowledges fault in failed trade for Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie

articles.body_text:
Nick Wright, Kevin Wildes, Greg Jennings and Danny Parkins discuss whether the Green Bay Packers' win says more about the New England Patriots or them, then Nick makes an announcement regarding the Cincinnati Bengals and Joe Burrow.

Bengals coach Zac Taylor acknowledged Cincinnati deserved blame after its failed attempt to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles before Tuesday’s trade deadline.

Taylor shared details Wednesday about how the process unfolded from the Bengals’ perspective, reading a prepared statement from Bengals director of football Duke Tobin. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me about how he wanted this portrayed," Taylor said as he began explaining why the roster move ultimately fell through. "I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked."

Tobin is the team's de facto general manager. He said the Bengals underestimated the cost of replacing Cashius Howell and emphasized that Philadelphia was a willing trade partner.

"We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear [that] Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor speaks at a news conference after an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns in Cincinnati, Ohio, on Jan. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Jeff Dean)

An initial report from NFL Network stated that the Bengals and Eagles decided on a deal that would send edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie to Cincinnati. The Bengals were set to give up a sixth-round pick in 2027, but the agreement apparently started going off the rails as the teams worked through the final details and tried to get the deal over the finish line.

MAXX CROSBY SAYS EVERYTHING HAPPENS FOR A REASON AFTER TRADE TO THE RAVENS FALLS THROUGH

ESPN reported Wednesday, citing sources, that it became clear to the Bengals that the team would need to give up a compensatory draft pick to finalize the trade. The additional compensation prompted Cincinnati back out of the proposed deal.

Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and director of player personnel Duke Tobin talk during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice field in downtown Cincinnati on Aug. 20, 2025. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

CHRISTIAN MCCAFFREY RECALLS 'WHIRLWIND' ORDEAL OF SHOCKING TRADE THAT SENT HIM FROM PANTHERS TO 49ERS

Questions remain about when and how the Bengals realized they would have to surrender the compensatory pick to complete the trade. The pick was awarded after Cincinnati lost more qualifying free agents than it signed, includingTrey Hendrickson.

Nick Korte posted on X about the potential loss of the pick after the trade was first reported as agreed to but before news emerged that the deal had fallen through.

Korte’s X profile identifies him as affiliated with OverTheCap, and he regularly shares NFL salary-cap news on the platform.

Taylor said he did not ask Tobin for details Tuesday because they did not matter to him.

"I didn't even ask the question," Taylor noted. "It doesn't really matter to me. It probably took three minutes of my day yesterday away from watching tape. Got a lot of faith in how [the front office] operates and we'll just move forward with it."

Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor walks on the sideline during the first half of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns in Cincinnati, Ohio, on Jan. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Joshua A. Bickel)

The Bengals defeated the Atlanta Falcons in the NFL’s first game in Madrid on Sunday to earn their fourth consecutive victory. Cincinnati hosts AFC North rival Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 10.

articles.title: Human torso found in sofa in Sydney bushland prompts homicide investigation
articles.excerpt:
Police called to Lane Cove North on Wednesday after sofa found containing human torso believed to be that of adult man

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales pol...
articles.body_text:
Police called to Lane Cove North on Wednesday after sofa found containing human torso believed to be that of adult man

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales police have launched a homicide investigation after a human torso was found in bushland on Sydney’s lower north shore.

Police were called to Lane Cove North about 2.30pm on Wednesday after reports of human remains.

Police had “received a number of reports from members of the public” regarding a strong odour in the area, Supt Paul Devaney told media on Thursday morning.

Officers found a sofa containing a human torso located about five metres off the roadway.

The remains consisted of “a torso … devoid of head, arms and legs”, Devaney said. There were signs the body had been there for “at least a couple of days”.

A crime scene was established, with forensic specialists seizing the human remains – believed to be that of an adult male – for a postmortem examination.

“It’s a very, very quiet street in Lane Cove, an area that has probably nil crime rate, so it’s a very unusual activity,” Devaney said.

Detectives together with the state’s homicide squad launched an investigation, with the Aviation Command (PolAir) and cadaver dog deployed.

Members of the public with information, including dashcam or security camera footage that may be relevant, were urged to contact police with information.

Devaney sought to reassure Lane Cove residents that there was no apparent threat to locals.

“There is no indication that this person met foul play within the area of Lane Cove. But it is very early stages in the investigation and we are still undertaking numerous and comprehensive inquiries,” he said.

articles.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least one and traps others in wreckage
articles.excerpt:
Four critical in hospital as firefighters dig through rubble in Flatbush after building next to construction site collapses

Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn o...
articles.body_text:
Four critical in hospital as firefighters dig through rubble in Flatbush after building next to construction site collapses

Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage.

Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section at about 4pm. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.

Two people died and four others were rushed to a hospital in critical condition, officials said in a Wednesday evening press conference. Twelve other patients were stable and one firefighter was treated for minor injuries. Seven children were among the patients.

Officials said they do not know how many people remain in the collapse site.

At about 6.30pm, firefighters pulled a dust-covered person – still alive and moving – out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting them up on a stretcher and rushing them to a waiting ambulance.

The building that collapsed had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.

Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.

A drone hovered over the site as firefighters dug by hand, tossing chunks of rubble aside. Rescuers also used rescue dogs to search for survivors.

As darkness fell, firefighters used flashlights to illuminate the area where they were working.

“As emergency operations continue, please join me in holding our neighbors and the members of this community in our hearts,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement posted on social media.

Phone and email messages seeking comment were left with the architect, property owner and general contractor listed in city records as being associated with the construction project.

articles.title: El-Sayed tells Hegseth to resign after impeachment effort fails: 'Make it easy for everybody'
articles.excerpt: Incoming Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed addresses Pete Hegseth directly on CNN, accusing the secretary of war of mismanaging military actions abroad and urging him to step aside after a failed House...
articles.body_text:
Incoming Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed addresses Pete Hegseth directly on CNN, accusing the secretary of war of mismanaging military actions abroad and urging him to step aside after a failed House impeachment vote.

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., called on Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to resign Tuesday, asking him, "Why are you still doing this job?"

Speaking with CNN's Kaitlan Collins, El-Sayed was asked whether Democrats should revive the failed impeachment attempt against Hegseth.

"Can you imagine being Pete Hegseth right now? Like, why are you still in your job? I mean it's an open question, like, 'Pete, like really, just open question, why are you still doing this job? You are really bad at this. You are failing your responsibility, you have mishandled this war and nobody really actually understands what it is you're about,'" El-Sayed said.

He spoke directly to the camera and said Hegseth was fighting a new culture war every day, but that he was supposed to be "waging an actual war that is actually illegal on its own terms."

DEMOCRATS RALLY BEHIND GOP LAWMAKER'S HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT PUSH, SIGNAL MORE TO COME IN JANUARY

Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed demanded Secretary of War Pete Hegseth resign during a CNN interview Tuesday. (Sarah Rice/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Pete Kiehart/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"So, just resign. Make it easy for everybody instead of, in the end, getting taken out because that is clearly what's happening. So, Pete, just take it from me. Like, you're not good at this," El-Sayed added.

House Republicans killed an impeachment effort led by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., on Tuesday, by voting 211-204 to refer the resolution to the House Judiciary Committee and avoid a full vote on impeachment.

All Democrats who voted opposed the motion, but 11 Democrats were absent.

President Donald Trump celebrated the failed impeachment effort in a Truth Social post, calling Massie a "total loser" and praising Hegseth's record on recruitment and military operations in Venezuela and Iran.

Collins asked El-Sayed during the CNN interview, "I mean you're talking directly to Pete Hegseth. What do you say to those 11 Democrats who didn't show up to vote tonight?"

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS

Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed addressed the secretary of war directly on CNN, saying he was failing in his responsibilities. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

El-Sayed told Democrats to show up and "do your job," and Collins said it was "surprising" that Democratic absences helped prevent a vote on the impeachment articles.

The Michigan senator-elect said he fielded questions from voters while on the campaign trail about high gas and grocery prices and attributed those costs to the war in Iran.

"Pete Hegseth has aided and abetted a president who we all know is way out of his league," he said. "And, so, you know, I think it is important for us to be recognizing that Pete Hegseth himself is the tie to the affordability that all of us crave when it comes to this administration.

"So, look, you know, obviously I'm not going to be in a position to vote to impeach, and I will assess any impeachment that is done on its own merits, but it's really quite clear that Pete Hegseth is failing his responsibilities as secretary of defense."

The White House and the Department of War did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

THE OVERLOOKED WAY THE IRAN WAR IS MAKING GROCERIES, AMAZON PACKAGES AND NEW HOMES MORE EXPENSIVE

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth speaks during a news conference at the Pentagon Nov. 10, 2026, in Arlington, Va. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Hegseth remained defiant during a news conference Tuesday, pushing back against the impeachment effort.

He said he stood behind military operations in Iran, Venezuela and Yemen, describing them as lawful.

"What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight. It's not accountability. It's a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment," Hegseth said.

"Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president, this country and, most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it."

Y. David Scharf, a government strategies and controversies attorney, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Democrats could spend the next two years trying to impeach Pete Hegseth and end up making him stronger.

"Congress may have every right to investigate, demand documents and subpoena witnesses," he continued. "But there’s a world of difference between holding an administration accountable and trying to remove someone simply because you don’t like his policies.

"Calling for Hegseth’s resignation is easy," Scharf added. "Actually removing him requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate. And if Democrats can’t even get their own members to show up for a vote, how do they expect to convince Republicans to join them?"

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Former Giants coach defends star player Malik Nabers against character questions from broadcast analyst

articles.body_text:
When his character came into question, Giants star wideout Malik Nabers took to social media to take on former player and TV analyst Greg Olsen, who criticized the receiver’s sideline demeanor during Sunday's broadcast.

One former New York Giants coach is running to Nabers' defense. Ex-Giants defensive coordinator Wink Martindale, who had a messy split with the team in 2024, harbors no bad blood toward the receiver and spoke up to defend Nabers against Olsen's critique.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

"I'm with Malik on this. Somebody put that in his ear, whether it's to keep his contract down for the next year when they want to extend him or whatever it is, I don't know. But just keep playing," Martindale said, appearing on Giants insider Pat Leonard's "Talkin' Ball" podcast.

Don Wink Martindale stands on the field before a game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minn., on Dec. 24, 2022. (Getty Images)

Broadcaster Greg Olsen looks on prior to the game between the Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field in Seattle, Wash., on Sept. 7, 2025. (Getty Images)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I love the kid. I love his competitiveness."

During the Giants' visit to Philadelphia on Sunday, Olsen and boothmate Joe Davis kept pointing to Nabers' "negative" body language on the sideline. They also called him out for pouting after a Giants drive finished with an Isaiah Likely touchdown.

"His body language has been terrible today," Davis said.

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (1) catches a pass as Dallas Cowboys cornerback Kaiir Elam (20) defends in the second half of an NFL football game Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/Jerome Miron)

KANSAS CITY CHIEFS STAR DEFENSIVE LINEMAN CHRIS JONES CAUGHT IN SCREAMING MATCH WITH COACHES ON SIDELINES

Olsen proved more frustrated with Nabers.

"I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot [of] really good players. There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That's great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates.

MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS

"So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You've just got to keep it in check."

Martindale added, "Think about all the great players that John Harbaugh's coached. Does he get blown up more because it's in New York? Of course it does. But it's nothing new for John."

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (1) looks on before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at MetLife Stadium on Sept 21, 2025. (Vincent Carchietta/Imagn Images)

Martindale knows a thing or two about friction inside New York's building. Following months of simmering tension during the 2023 season, his Giants tenure imploded in January 2024 after head coach Brian Daboll fired Martindale’s trusted defensive assistants. Martindale reportedly cursed out Daboll, stormed out, and mutually parted ways.

Despite showing visible frustration during the Giants' 19-11 win in Philadelphia, where he had five catches for 43 yards after four straight 100-yard games, Nabers' commitment was never questioned by his locker room.

Giants players publicly defended him as a "good teammate, " with running back Cam Skattebo noting that Nabers' sideline annoyance when lacking targets simply reflects a competitive edge teammates "love to see."

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: El Salvador-backed air assault destroys Haiti gang headquarters amid search for missing troops

El Salvador’s president said the operation destroyed a major Haiti gang’s headquarters believed to be used for kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion. (@nayibbukele/X)

El Salvador's president...
articles.body_text:
El Salvador’s president said the operation destroyed a major Haiti gang’s headquarters believed to be used for kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion. (@nayibbukele/X)

El Salvador's president on Tuesday said the country's military helped deliver a devastating air assault against the headquarters of one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs, which has been linked to mass kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion.

Airstrikes targeted strongholds belonging to 400 Mawozo and the home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said.

The attack took place Sunday near Port-au-Prince and was carried out by a Haitian police task force backed by Salvadoran troops, The Miami Herald reported.

BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR

El Salvador’s president said the operation destroyed a major Haiti gang’s headquarters used for kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion. (@nayibbukele/X)

The operation appears to be part of an ongoing military effort in response to the disappearance of four Salvadoran members of a U.N.-backed security mission abducted in a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince Oct. 18.

"We kept our promise," Bukele said in a post on X.

Videos showed several helicopters launching airstrikes against multiple compounds inside sprawling complexes. Dozens of people were also seen fleeing the properties on foot and motorbikes after the strikes.

"Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!" Bukele said.

As many as 20 people are believed to have been killed in the operation, according to The Miami Herald, citing anonymous sources.

SUSPECTS IN HAITIAN PRESIDENT'S ASSASSINATION TRANSFERRED TO MIAMI, ACCUSED OF FUNDING PLOT WITH COVID FRAUD

Dozens of people run through the area after a helicopter strike targeting a gang headquarters in Haiti. (@nayibbukele/X)

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé on Tuesday thanked Bukele for his commitment to tackling the country's long-running gang crisis and restoring state control, while praising the efforts of the U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the Haitian National Police, the Haitian Armed Forces and their international partners.

"I salute the commitment of the Salvadoran forces in the fight against gangs," he said.

"Hats off to President Nayib Bukele @nayibbukele for your support and commitment to the national fight against gangs. Haiti, El Salvador, GSF: same fight, same determination! The collaboration will continue. THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!"

Black smoke rises across a field after a helicopter strike targeting a major gang’s headquarters in Haiti. (@nayibbukele/X)

After an Oct. 18 ambush, authorities recovered a burned armored vehicle with no trace of the four missing Salvadoran personnel, prompting El Salvador to deploy thousands of additional troops to assist in the search.

While Salvadoran officials believe the men were abducted and survived, one gang leader claimed they were dead.

The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: Former Italian Red Brigades member escapes house arrest in Argentina
articles.excerpt: A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s far-left Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina by climbing down from a fifth-floor apartment using a harness and rope, prompting a nationwide s...
articles.body_text:
A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s far-left Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina by climbing down from a fifth-floor apartment using a harness and rope, prompting a nationwide search.

Leonardo Bertulazzi, who faces extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence, escaped on Tuesday and was still on the run on Wednesday, Argentine police officials told The Associated Press news agency.

Bertulazzi was convicted in absentia by a court in his home country for his role in the kidnapping and death of a former Italian prime minister by the left-wing armed group, and his refugee status in Argentina was revoked under right-wing President Javier Milei.

Police said he descended onto the second-floor terrace of a neighbouring house, climbed down to a first-floor terrace, crossed a vacant lot and got onto the street by climbing over a gate.

Authorities did not immediately notice Bertulazzi was gone as he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor, the officials said. They said he placed it inside a device containing a thermal blanket to maintain its temperature, along with grease or animal fat, apparently to keep moisture in.

Explosives specialists examined the device, which had been made to resemble an explosive.

Argentina’s Security Ministry has offered a reward of 20 million pesos (about $13,000) for information leading to his capture.

The Red Brigades were a far-left armed group responsible for a wave of kidnappings and killings in Italy in the 1970s and 1980s, a period known as the “Years of Lead”.

The group kidnapped and killed former Prime Minister Aldo Moro in 1978. Argentine authorities have said Bertulazzi, who belonged to the group’s Genoa branch, was involved in the logistics of Moro’s kidnapping.

Italian courts convicted him in the 1980s of “terrorism-related” crimes, resulting in a combined 27-year sentence, according to Argentine court records.

He was first arrested in Buenos Aires in November 2002, but an Argentine judge rejected Italy’s extradition request in 2003 because Italian law did not guarantee him a new trial after a conviction in absentia. He was granted refugee status in 2004.

Argentina revoked it in 2024, under Milei, and re-arrested him that August. Its Supreme Court approved his extradition last year.

Wanda Ferro, an undersecretary in Italy’s Interior Ministry, said Argentine police were responsible for ensuring he was handed over. “I am certain that every effort will be made,” she told local television, adding that she hoped the extradition could take place “very quickly” if Bertulazzi is recaptured.

articles.title: Australian states could sue tobacco companies for billions in healthcare costs under proposal
articles.excerpt:
Exclusive: Former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer argues states could seek up to $50bn in compensation

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily n...
articles.body_text:
Exclusive: Former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer argues states could seek up to $50bn in compensation

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian state governments could sue tobacco companies for billions in public hospital and healthcare costs, under a proposal developed by a former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer.

The South Australian government is formally seeking advice on the proposal, while other states are reviewing it.

Authored by Sydney Health Law research affiliate Neil Francey, the proposal argues the states could file proceedings in the federal court seeking up to $50bn in compensation for health costs, and to fund cancer screening programs and prevention measures.

It targets the dominant tobacco companies in Australia – British American Tobacco (BAT), Philip Morris and Imperial Brands – and their parent corporations overseas.

Francey is presenting the blueprint at the Clinical Oncology Society of Australia’s annual scientific meeting in Sydney on Thursday, arguing the companies could be held liable for decades of misleading and deceptive conduct under Australian consumer law.

He has also briefed state government MPs. Under the plan, the six state governments would pool their resources to set up a dedicated, joint legal taskforce to run the case.

“For decades, the tobacco industry has unjustly enriched itself while distracting and confusing smokers about the harms and addictiveness of their product,” the proposal says.

“The industry has not been forced to bear the full costs of the harm caused by their product. These costs have either been borne by smokers themselves, or by taxpayers when smokers get sick and receive publicly funded or subsidised health care.”

A BAT Australia spokesperson said the company does not comment on potential or pending legal claims, while Philip Morris and Imperial Brands did not respond to requests for comment.

Francey told Guardian Australia that the proposal excludes the Northern Territory and the ACT, as the territories are an arm of the commonwealth, and there are differences in healthcare funding arrangements that could complicate the case.

The proposal seeks to recover healthcare costs incurred by the states since 2000, when internal tobacco industry documents were published revealing the industry knew that smoking caused serious diseases but colluded to cover up and obfuscate the evidence.

“I think you can justify a figure in the order of fifty billion, possibly even more,” Francey said.

In 1991, Francey represented consumers in a federal court of Australia case triggered by a Tobacco Institute of Australia advertisement that claimed there was “nothing which proves scientifically that cigarette smoke causes disease in nonsmokers”.

The court found compelling scientific proof that passive smoking causes lung disease and respiratory conditions in non-smokers, making the industry’s claims unlawful. The historic ruling accelerated workplace and public indoor smoking bans.

Francey said his latest proposal has the benefit of being brought by state governments under consumer protection laws, bypassing some of the challenges faced by smokers pursuing personal injury lawsuits, where it can be hard to prove which brand caused the harm, and with tobacco companies arguing people have “freedom of choice”.

Francey said state governments could seek court orders against companies engaged in misleading and deceptive conduct which has led to loss and damage and the likelihood of suffering in future.

The South Australian health minister, Blair Boyer, said there was a “substantial” public interest in measures reducing the harms that tobacco-related diseases place on governments, health systems and communities.

“While this proposal draws on historic findings regarding misleading and deceptive conduct by the tobacco industry, it is important that the state does its own due diligence,” he said.

“I have sought advice on the proposal, the likelihood of success and the benefits to South Australians, which will allow the government to consider its options.”

A spokesperson for the NSW health minister, Ryan Park, said: “We will review his proposal carefully”.

A spokesperson for the Queensland health minister, Tim Nicholls, confirmed a meeting with Francey, but said the state was focused on laws targeting the illicit tobacco and vape trade. The Western Australian health minister, Meredith Hammat, said the state’s efforts are currently focused on strengthening tobacco legislation and enforcement activities.

The CEO of the Australian Council on Smoking & Health, Laura Hunter, said it would be “entirely reasonable for tobacco companies to bear the costs of the harm their products have caused” in Australia.

“For years, they’ve made money selling products that addict people and cause serious illness and death,” she said. “The responsibility for addressing that harm belongs with the companies that profited from it.”

The legal push follows cases overseas, including the landmark 1998 Master Settlement Agreement signed by major US tobacco companies and state attorneys general to settle dozens of lawsuits seeking to recover billions in smoking-related healthcare costs.

In 2025, three of the biggest tobacco companies were ordered to pay billions in compensation for smoking-related harms in Canada, though health groups expressed disappointment that the decision did not address harms from future use.

A professor of tobacco control with the University of Sydney, Becky Freeman, said the Canadian case was protracted over many years, and that any country taking on tobacco companies needed to ensure they were on “solid ground” to avoid spiralling costs and lacklustre outcomes.

“I am absolutely supportive of the tobacco industry being held accountable,” she said.

“I would want to ensure any action was comprehensive.”

Associate Prof Jonathan Liberman, an expert in law and global health at the University of Melbourne who has spent more than two decades working on legal aspects of tobacco control, said what has made tobacco litigation challenging is the scale and duration of the tobacco industry’s wrongdoing, and how vigorously the industry has defended it.

A range of features of the US legal system make large-scale litigation easier there, he said. To be successful in Australia, litigation against the tobacco industry over the health costs of smoking would need specific enabling legislation, and well resourced law firms working outside government doing the bulk of the necessary legal work, he said.

“Without these, lawsuits risk consuming significant time and public resources that may be better directed toward direct policy reform, and ultimately falling over on a combination of procedural grounds and resources running out.”

articles.title: Illegal immigrant arrested after dragging, striking ICE officer in Chicago suburb: DHS
articles.excerpt: Criminal defense attorney Josh Ritter and former NYPD Lt. Darrin Porcher react to the New Jersey incident in which an illegal alien allegedly rammed an ICE agent. They emphasize the staggering 3,300% ...
articles.body_text:
Criminal defense attorney Josh Ritter and former NYPD Lt. Darrin Porcher react to the New Jersey incident in which an illegal alien allegedly rammed an ICE agent. They emphasize the staggering 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks against law enforcement officers.

FIRST ON FOX: An illegal immigrant with a prior criminal history was arrested Wednesday after allegedly dragging a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer with his car while fleeing an arrest attempt outside Chicago, federal officials said.

Jose Garnica-Naranjo, 32, a Mexican citizen, was taken into custody a day after violently resisting a targeted immigration enforcement operation, according to the Department of Homeland Security.

"This illegal alien used his vehicle to assault one of our ICE officers, hospitalizing the officer," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

"Thankfully, the officer has since been released from the hospital. This is just the latest example of the staggering rise in anti-ICE violence, with our officers facing a more than 1,600% increase in assaults against them."

Photos provided to Fox News Digital appeared to show the ICE officer's wounded leg following the incident. (DHS)

VENEZUELAN NATIONAL SHOT BY ICE OFFICER IN AUSTIN CHARGED WITH ASSAULTING FEDERAL OFFICER

ICE officers spotted Garnica-Naranjo leaving a home in Chicago Heights on Tuesday morning. Officers followed his car at a distance before attempting to initiate a traffic stop, DHS said.

When officers approached the vehicle, they instructed Garnica-Naranjo to turn off the engine, but he allegedly refused to comply.

"When officers attempted to remove him from the vehicle, Garnica accelerated and fled while an ERO Chicago officer was partially inside the vehicle through the driver-side window," DHS said in a statement.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents walk down a street during a multi-agency targeted enforcement operation in Chicago Jan. 26, 2025. (Christopher Dilts/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

ICE SAYS OFFICER SHOT AND KILLED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO TRIED TO RAM HIM WITH CAR IN HOUSTON

Garnica-Naranjo then drove over a raised center median planted with trees, causing the officer to be thrown from the vehicle, according to authorities.

As Garnica-Naranjo fled, his car struck the injured officer, who was subsequently taken to a local hospital. The officer suffered contusions, cuts and scrapes to his legs, though tests confirmed no broken bones.

ICE noted that Garnica-Naranjo's criminal record includes prior convictions for domestic violence and assault.

Mullin blamed violence against immigration officers on rhetoric from Democratic elected officials who have accused ICE of terrorizing neighborhoods during law enforcement operations.

"This is the result of anti-ICE rhetoric from sanctuary politicians like Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker," he said. "DHS is calling on Governor Pritzker and all other sanctuary politicians to knock off this violent rhetoric and start cooperating with ICE before any more officers are injured in the line of duty."

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Jamie Foxx’s daughter’s 18th birthday bash erupts in violence as deputies make arrests
articles.excerpt:
Jamie Foxx attended the 2025 Golden Globe Awards as a nominee for his Netflix comedy special, ‘Jamie Foxx: What Happened Was...’

A birthday celebration for Jamie Foxx's daughter descended into chaos ...
articles.body_text:
Jamie Foxx attended the 2025 Golden Globe Awards as a nominee for his Netflix comedy special, ‘Jamie Foxx: What Happened Was...’

A birthday celebration for Jamie Foxx's daughter descended into chaos when violent fights erupted Nov. 7.

The violence unfolded during SKVLK Fest, an annual Halloween music festival held at Foxx's California mansion. The party was reportedly coordinated by his daughter, Anelise, who turned 18 Oct. 3.

Originally scheduled for Halloween, the event was postponed because of rain.

Video obtained by TMZ from the music festival-turned-birthday bash shows a fight that broke out among guests. Several people were seen punching each other and rolling around on the ground.

JAMIE FOXX THINKS 'GOD SOMETIMES SLIPS AWAY' IN HOLLYWOOD

Video obtained by TMZ showed multiple partygoers throwing punches and wrestling on the ground during the event at Jamie Foxx's home. (Christopher Polk/Getty Images)

The Ventura County Sheriff's Department later confirmed multiple physical altercations took place during the party.

"It was reported to Sheriff’s Communications that a male juvenile suspect allegedly slashed another male juvenile with a knife, causing a response from patrol deputies," a statement shared by authorities read.

"Once on scene, deputies and investigators were told a juvenile victim suffered a superficial laceration to the victim’s neck believed to be from a knife."

After investigating, the Ventura County Sheriff's Department determined the victim was not assaulted with a knife and that his injury appeared to have resulted from a physical altercation.

Authorities said an estimated 3,000 or more people attended the event.

A "Party and Premise Rules" sign is seen at Jamie Foxx’s California home during SKVLK Fest Nov. 7. The event, which doubled as a birthday celebration for Foxx’s daughter, Anelise, was marked by multiple physical altercations, authorities said. (TMZ)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

SKVLK Fest was held Nov. 7 and doubled as an 18th birthday celebration for Jamie Foxx's daughter. (Earl Gibson III/Getty Images)

While authorities were at Foxx's home responding to the initial call, they witnessed a juvenile kick another individual in the head. The suspect was taken into custody.

The following day, a third victim reported he was assaulted near the concert stage after being knocked to the ground in a mosh pit, according to the police statement. He said he was repeatedly punched and kicked before losing consciousness. He also reported his phone and money had been stolen. His phone was later recovered and returned.

The Ventura County Sheriff's Department is seeking video from the party as the investigations continue. So far, two juvenile suspects have been arrested.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The Ventura County Sheriff's Department confirmed multiple physical altercations and arrests. (Marc Piasecki/Getty Images for Amend)

"We're grateful to the Ventura County Sheriff's deputies and detectives for their thorough work and to the EMTs and security staff who responded quickly that night," the festival said in a statement issued through PR STARPOWER, which handles sponsorships and partnerships for SKVLK Fest.

"Our thoughts are with everyone who was hurt, and we’re cooperating fully as the investigations continue," the statement continued. "But the record needs to be clear: no one was stabbed."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Anelise Foxx is Jamie Foxx's daughter, whom he shares with his former partner Kristin Grannis. (Etitnne Laurent/AFP via Getty Images)

It's unclear whether Foxx was at the party. The actor has been filming in Australia, according to his latest Instagram posts.

Fox News Digital reached out to Foxx's representative for more information.

SKVLK Fest is an annual Halloween-themed music and carnival festival reportedly organized by Anelise. What began as a family celebration has grown into a large entertainment event featuring celebrity performances, carnival rides, costumes and social media personalities.

The festival has attracted major hip-hop and R&B performers. Its 2026 lineup included Offset, OhGeesy, 310babii and SuperDuperKyle. Previous performers have included GloRilla, Tyga, Ty Dolla $ign, Sexyy Red and YK Osiris.

articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
articles.excerpt:
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.

Colom's victory makes...
articles.body_text:
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.

Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years.

Only a few thousand votes separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.

The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called.

Colom won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS.

Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well.

"While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said.

Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced.

The room burst into deafening applause and cheers.

"This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board.

"This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising.

Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory.

"When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy."

Colom supporters celebrate his win in Jackson, Mississippi

The result wipes away a Republican winning streak in the Magnolia State that dates back to 1982.

The contest was never expected to be this close, with Hyde-Smith running for re-election in a state that President Donald Trump won in the 2024 election by more than 22 points.

But Democrats have scored a series of major wins in these midterm elections, taking control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

The party flipped Senate seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.

Polls suggest this was due in large part to voter frustrations with the economy and the Iran war under President Trump.

Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans.

Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls.

Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices".

The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties.

Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns.

The Republican was criticised for a lack of public appearances.

articles.title: Jeffries leaves door open to investigating major Trump ally as Democrats prepare to take power
articles.excerpt: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was not opposed to an Elon Musk probe as threats to investigate the former head of DOGE continue to loom after Democrats took back both majorities in Congress. (C...
articles.body_text:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was not opposed to an Elon Musk probe as threats to investigate the former head of DOGE continue to loom after Democrats took back both majorities in Congress. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digital)

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries left the door open to a congressional investigation into Elon Musk as threats to probe both the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and other Trump allies continue to heat up under a new Democratic House majority.

"We're going to follow the facts," Jeffries said about the potential investigation. "We're going to apply the law. We're gonna be guided by the Constitution."

Musk has emerged as a potential target of Democratic oversight, with some lawmakers calling for scrutiny of his time as head of the DOGE.

The calls for an investigation come as Democrats have started rallying the party to look into alleged corruption under the Trump administration after coming out victorious in midterms.

SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE

President Donald Trump's friendship with Elon Musk is warming up again as the president reignites praise and mentions of Musk in public. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

Asked whether Musk should be investigated by the new Democratic majority, Jeffries declined to commit to a probe, instead pointing to the lawmakers expected to lead the party's oversight efforts.

"Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia are going to lead our oversight efforts," Jeffries told Fox News Digital. "And I defer to them at the moment."

Raskin, D-Md., has already signaled that DOGE could face congressional scrutiny, telling Fox News Digital last week he believes an investigation is warranted, even as he acknowledged having no specific plan.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

"I had no specific plan," Raskin told Fox News Digital about the potential investigations. "Look … DOGE was a catastrophe for America, and at least one committee, I feel pretty certain, will investigate it. It needs to investigate it."

After taking the majority, the prospects for new investigations come with Raskin and Garcia positioned to be chairs of the House Judiciary and Oversight Committees.

Raskin, Garcia, Jeffries and Assistant Democratic Leader Joe Neguse have already begun strategizing plans for the investigative agenda.

Jeffries is in the running for speaker of the House after formally announcing his bid just a day after Democrats took back the majority in the midterm elections. Democrats have not been united in their decision to back Jeffries or another candidate to represent the party as House speaker.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: HOUSE LEADERSHIP UP FOR GRABS AS GOP RECKONS WITH DEVASTATING LOSSES

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks alongside Rep. Pete Aguilar and Rep. Katherine Clark during a news conference in Washington, D.C., Jan. 8, 2026. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Leadership elections for House Democrats will be held Nov. 18 and members will vote with "secret ballots" to keep their individual nominations private.

Jeffries will need a simple majority of Democrats to be nominated, but to be formally elected as House speaker, he’ll need to get 218 floor votes.

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.
