articles.title: Pete Hegseth faces impeachment effort as Republican lawmaker moves to force vote – US politics live
articles.excerpt:
Thomas Massie, Republican congressman, accuses defense secretary of illegally waging war without congressional authorization

Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Pete Hegseth

As I...
articles.body_text:
Thomas Massie, Republican congressman, accuses defense secretary of illegally waging war without congressional authorization

Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Pete Hegseth

As I noted earlier, Thomas Massie’s push to Pete Hegseth has been months in the making.

In September, Massie introduced the articles, but was stopped when Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson ended up cancelling the final day of votes ahead of the midterms recess. For Massie, an outgoing Republican who lost his primary election earlier this year, he has long pushed back against the lack of congressional approval for the administration’s war in Iran.

“I’m a defeated congressman. I’m not disgruntled, and we’ll see if the plan works,” he said on Tuesday. “I’m being polite here … An impeachment is just firing somebody. Really, you don’t go to prison. You don’t go to jail. You’re not. You don’t pay a fine.”

Now that Massie has refiled the resolution, the House has two days to take it up. This could result in a vote on the floor, a formal investigation or the measure could be tabled. All require a simple majority (218 votes) in the House.

While the Iran conflict is the primary focus of the articles of impeachment, Massie’s resolution also focuses on Hegseth’s move to strike several boats in the Caribbean that have killed over 200 people throughout the campaign.

“Not only are they striking people without identifying them,” Massie told reporters after speaking on the House floor. “They don’t know who all those people are in the boat. They’re going back and killing all the survivors. This puts our own military in danger in any kind of future military engagement.”

The resolution also points to the defense secretary’s targeted Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, a former Navy captain, for telling troops to resist unlawful orders. Hegseth formally censured Kelly, accused him of seditious statements, and moved to reduce his retired military rank and pension. A federal judge later blocked the Pentagon’s effort.

Today, Massie said that Hegseth is in more danger when Democrats take over Congress in the new year.

“They won’t have just eight articles of impeachment,” the congressman said. “I suspect if Pete Hegseth doesn’t leave … the Democrats are going to bring people in here who have served under him and with him, give them protection. They’ll be able to say what he’s actually done, the things he has ignored, the things that he did that caused civilian casualties, the way he’s you know ignored the laws, and then there’ll be a full robust trial over in the Senate.”

Massie added: “And it’s not a certain thing that he would survive the Senate, you know, even though you know they don’t have what would you call it an impeachment-proof majority in the Senate.”

A reminder that for the removal of an impeached official, there needs to be 67 votes in the upper chamber.

Speaking to reporters, Massie insisted that his articles of impeachment are “not symbolic”.

“He is not doing a good job. In addition to breaking the law and violating the constitution, he’s not doing a good job,” Massie said. “If he stays in power, and Republicans reject this – what message do you think he sends to the American public after last week’s election?

Republican Congressman Thomas Massie has introduced eight articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth, refiling a resolution in the hope of ousting the defense secretary. The House has two days to take it up. This could result in a vote on the floor, a formal investigation or the measure could be tabled. All require a simple majority (218 votes) in the House.

Massie, the outgoing representative from Kentucky, accused Hegseth of illegally waging war in Iran without congressional authorization and abusing his powers. The articles also focuses on Hegseth’s move to strike several boats in the Caribbean that have killed over 200 people throughout the campaign. The resolution also points to the defense secretary’s targeted Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, a former Navy captain, for telling troops to resist unlawful orders. Hegseth formally censured Kelly, accused him of seditious statements, and moved to reduce his retired military rank and pension. A federal judge later blocked the Pentagon’s effort.

While Democrats are expected to back the impeachment effort, some Republicans have also expressed some support, even though they hold a narrow majority. A reminder that for the removal of an impeached official, there needs to be 67 votes in the upper chamber. Speaking to reporters, Massie insisted that his articles of impeachment are “not symbolic”. “He is not doing a good job. In addition to breaking the law and violating the constitution, he’s not doing a good job,” Massie said. “If he stays in power, and Republicans reject this – what message do you think he sends to the American public after last week’s election?”

After initially saying he would accept the results of the midterm elections, that saw Democrats flip dozens of seats and win control of Congress, Donald Trump has begun to cast doubt on the Republican drubbing. “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” he wrote on Truth Social. “How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote.” The president also repeated his baseless aspersions that that voting machines are unreliable. “It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” Trump wrote.

Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer responded to Trump’s statement, saying that the president’s “return to election denialism was inevitable”. The Senate minority leader added: “He can whine all he wants, but nothing will stop this inescapable truth: For the last two years of his presidency, Trump will face the largest Democratic congressional majorities in decades, all because he has been an unprecedented failure.”

Could Hakeem Jeffries, as the likely next speaker of the House, work with Stephen Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign who last week named White House chief of staff?

“No”, Jeffries replied, when asked about the possibility of collaboration at his press conference today.

“Stephen Miller is a stone cold racist. His track record speaks for itself, and I’ve got zero interest in working with that kind of individual,” Jeffries added.

It’s not the first time the top House Democrat has condemned Miller, but this language is Jeffries’s strongest yet. Needless to say, this does not bode well for the possibility of bipartisan collaboration in the next Congress on issues like immigration reform.

Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer, the top Democrats in the House and Senate, respectively, may have just led their party to historic victories in the midterm elections, but they remain unpopular with the party’s base.

Activists have called on House and Senate Democrats to elect other leaders before they assume the majorities in Congress next year. At a press conference today, Jeffries signaled confidence in Schumer’s chances of staying on as the top Senate Democrat.

“Chuck Schumer was the quarterback of a team effort led by Senate Democrats and incredible candidates who ran all across the country,” Jeffries said.

“I think the results of that election, the outcome, the decisive victory, speaks for itself.”

He was more diplomatic about his own chances of staying on as the top House Democrat – and thereby speaker of the House in waiting – ahead of caucus leadership meetings set for Wednesday and Thursday of next week.

“I’m going to work hard to talk to every single member about what we’ve been able to do together over the last two years and what the opportunities are for us to do together in the next two years to deliver upon the dramatic change that the American people so decisively voted for this past Tuesday,” Jeffries said.

When a reporter said it sounded like Jeffries didn’t have the votes “nailed down,” he replied: “You think I don’t have the vote nailed down? … I guess we’ll find out next Wednesday.”

Massie said today that he hopes that Pete Hegseth addresses the resolution methodically at his Pentagon press conference, scheduled for tomorrow.

“I hope he addresses the eight articles and doesn’t get up and misquote the Bible in Quentin Tarantino fashion and do some pull-ups and you know call everybody fat and gay like for being for this impeachment,” Massie said. “I may have just given you half his speech. I don’t know, but I would like to see him go through the eight articles of impeachment and just make the argument from a podium.”

Now that Massie has refiled the resolution, the House has two days to take it up. This could result in a vote on the floor, a formal investigation or the measure could be tabled. All require a simple majority (218 votes) in the House.

While the Iran conflict is the primary focus of the articles of impeachment, Massie’s resolution also focuses on Hegseth’s move to strike several boats in the Caribbean that have killed over 200 people throughout the campaign.

“Not only are they striking people without identifying them,” Massie told reporters after speaking on the House floor. “They don’t know who all those people are in the boat. They’re going back and killing all the survivors. This puts our own military in danger in any kind of future military engagement.”

The resolution also points to the defense secretary’s targeted Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, a former Navy captain, for telling troops to resist unlawful orders. Hegseth formally censured Kelly, accused him of seditious statements, and moved to reduce his retired military rank and pension. A federal judge later blocked the Pentagon’s effort.

Today, Massie said that Hegseth is in more danger when Democrats take over Congress in the new year.

“They won’t have just eight articles of impeachment,” the congressman said. “I suspect if Pete Hegseth doesn’t leave … the Democrats are going to bring people in here who have served under him and with him, give them protection. They’ll be able to say what he’s actually done, the things he has ignored, the things that he did that caused civilian casualties, the way he’s you know ignored the laws, and then there’ll be a full robust trial over in the Senate.”

Massie added: “And it’s not a certain thing that he would survive the Senate, you know, even though you know they don’t have what would you call it an impeachment-proof majority in the Senate.”

A reminder that for the removal of an impeached official, there needs to be 67 votes in the upper chamber.

Speaking to reporters, Massie insisted that his articles of impeachment are “not symbolic”.

“He is not doing a good job. In addition to breaking the law and violating the constitution, he’s not doing a good job,” Massie said. “If he stays in power, and Republicans reject this – what message do you think he sends to the American public after last week’s election?

Senator Chuck Schumer, who is hoping to become the upper chamber’s majority leader when Democrats take control in the new year, is now facing pushback from members of his party for the top job.

Many Democratic lawmakers are pushing for new leadership, and a generational shift given the historic victories the party secured in the midterm elections.

“We need a conversation about leadership going forward because we need new energy and ideas,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat, on Monday.

Over the weekend, several other caucus members questioned whether Schumer, 75, who currently serves as the minority leader, should go unchallenged.

“I’ve been very vocal that we need a new generation of leadership. We couldn’t have gotten a clearer signal than Tuesday,” said Elissa Slotkin, a first-term Democrat from Michigan. Meanwhile, sources close to Chris Van Hollen, the progressive Maryland senator, say that the lawmaker is receiving “an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode” about throwing his hat in the ring for leader, according to Politico.

Several freshmen Democrats spent time on the campaign trail insisting that they would not support Schumer as leader. This includes the Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who won the bitter fight for the open US Senate seat in Michigan, who only secured Schumer’s support after he won the Democratic primary against Haley Stevens, who Schumer backed initially. Other Senate newcomers, Troy Jackson of Maine, Adam Hamilton of Kansas and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, have all said they would support a different leader.

We’re watching the latest on the House floor, where Republican Thomas Massie is introducing eight articles of impeachment against defense secretary Pete Hegseth. Massie is hoping to force a vote, which could happen as soon as Wednesday.

Part of the impeachment articles includes the claim that Hegseth “abused the powers of the Department of Defense” that, he claims, resulted in the death of more than 175 civilians after strikes on an elementary school in Minab, Iran in February. The Pentagon has not confirmed responsibility for the specific attack, despite independent analyses finding the US was behind the strikes.

The defense department has carried out its own investigation, with a preliminary inquiry showing Washington responsible the deadly missile strike, according to a New York Times report.

After news emerged about the relationship between Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO and founder, and Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese government spy, several tech and business moguls shared their support of the Nvidia leader.

Elon Musk posted “I agree” in response to prominent venture capitalist Shaun Maguire’s defense of Huang. Maguire argued the Nvidia CEO “did something incredibly dumb” but that he is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation”.

“Two mistakes don’t make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” Maguire posted. He stated the Nvidia CEO “did something incredibly dumb” but that he is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation”.

“Let’s also not nuke our AI industry because China ran a successful intel op,” Maguire added in a separate post.

Bill Ackman, the US hedge fund manager and pro-Trump billionaire, meanwhile, suggested that Huang is “human” and deserves public support over the affair.

“He is an incredible human. Even incredible humans make mistakes,” Ackman posted. “He takes full responsibility as he should. We should all support him and his family. Onward.”

Ackman followed up with another post later clarifying that he wasn’t suggesting Huang “gets a free pass” but that he was “hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security”.

In the House tomorrow, we’ll also see leadership elections for the Republican conference. Here, outgoing GOP Speaker Mike Johnson said he will not run as minority leader.

Now, a contest between Representative Steve Scalise, the current majority leader, and hardline Congressman Jim Jordan is shaping up, as they both announced bids to lead Republicans in the next Congress.

Several Republican senators have called on party leadership to delay the internal election scheduled for tomorrow (Tuesday).

“We need to have serious discussions within our conference as to what we can do to improve the outcome in 2028,” the group wrote in a letter to conference chair Senator Tom Cotton, noting the stunning GOP defeat in the midterm elections last week. “Holding leadership elections without engaging in a robust discussion and evaluation of how those running for leadership intend to lead would be political malpractice. It is certainly not the way leadership elections should be conducted in the world’s greatest deliberative body.”

Senator Ron Johnson, of Wisconsin, led the letter. However, there is no apparent challenger to the upper chamber’s majority leader, Senator John Thune. If Thune stays in place, he will lead the Republican minority in the next Congress.

Thomas Massie, the outgoing Republican congressman, is re-introducing his eight articles of impeachment today against Pete Hegseth, in his bid to oust the defense secretary.

Massie, who lost his primary earlier this year, will likely move to force an impeachment vote against Hegseth again, ahead of Democrats re-taking control of Congress in the new year.

The articles include launching and continuing an unauthorized war in Iran, violating the War Powers Resolution without seeking congressional approval.

As we noted earlier, many House Democrats appear in lock-step behind the impeachment resolution. On Sunday, House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries said he was a “hard yes” on the vote.

Democrats have flipped the Georgia state House, the Associated Press reported on Monday.

As of Monday, Democrats had won 91 House seats and Republicans 86, per the AP.

The state House in Georgia has been Republican-controlled since 2005. The flip comes as Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship in Georgia last week.

articles.title: Suspect in Charlie Kirk killing to stand trial for murder in July 2028
articles.excerpt:
Utah judge sets timeline for trial of Tyler Robinson, accused of fatally shooting the far-right activist in September 2025

Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old man accused of killing the far-right pundit ...
articles.body_text:
Utah judge sets timeline for trial of Tyler Robinson, accused of fatally shooting the far-right activist in September 2025

Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old man accused of killing the far-right pundit and activist Charlie Kirk, will stand trial for murder in early July 2028, a Utah district judge ruled on Monday.

Judge Tony Graf said the trial will remain in Provo, Utah, and jury selection would begin on 21 June 2028. Attorneys for Robinson had asked to start the trial in January 2029 while Erika Kirk, Charlie’s widow, had pushed for an October 2027 date.

Last September, according to prosecutors, Tyler Robinson perched on a rooftop on Utah Valley University’s campus, where he opened fire on Kirk, who was in the middle of one of his signature debates with ideological rivals on college campuses.

Prosecutors say Robinson harbored grievances against Kirk’s political views, particularly the conservative figure’s criticism of gay rights.

Robinson turned himself in after the shooting, according to police, but has since pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder. If convicted of the charge, he could face the death penalty.

Prosecutors also charged Robinson with two counts of witness tampering for allegedly instructing his roommate to not cooperate with police and to delete incriminating texts, and two counts of obstruction of justice, according to court documents.

Robinson’s trial date had been a source of contention. In October, Robinson’s legal team reportedly proposed that the trial be held in the third quarter of 2029. They pointed to the sizable evidence in the case and jury selection preparations as reasons for needing additional time.

Lawyers for Erika Kirk, the widow of Charlie Kirk, balked at the defense attorney’s proposal in court filings.

Donald Trump also weighed in on the matter, writing last month on social media: “This case should be tried within a month, not three years – and it should be over with!”

He took a jab at Tony Graf, the Utah district judge presiding over the case, saying Graf was “desecrating the memory of the Great Charlie Kirk, while taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to”.

At the trial, prosecutors are expected to present evidence of Robinson seemingly confessing to the crime. During a July preliminary hearing, the court watched a redacted video in which Lance Twiggs, Robinson’s former roommate, told investigators that Robinson expressed regret about the shooting. “He wishes he hadn’t done it,” said Twiggs, who had also dated Robinson.

The hearing offered hints of how Robinson’s attorneys will defend him. They cast doubt over whether there was sufficient evidence to back the state’s motive theory – that Robinson had deep-set political differences with Kirk. They also scrutinized the reliability of forensic evidence, which indicated Robinson’s DNA on a towel wrapped around a firearm.

articles.title: Cyprus rivals agree new crossings across island’s dividing line
articles.excerpt: Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders have agreed ⁠to open two ⁠new border crossings, coordinate emergency responses, and share archival materials as part of a United Nations-backed effort to resu...
articles.body_text:
Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders have agreed ⁠to open two ⁠new border crossings, coordinate emergency responses, and share archival materials as part of a United Nations-backed effort to resume ⁠peace talks on the divided island.

Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman jointly met with United Nations special envoy Maria Angela Holguin on Monday in the UN-controlled buffer zone that splits the island. The agreement is the first concrete sign of detente between the rivals after nearly a decade of deadlock.

The UN said in a statement that Monday’s meeting was “positive” and that the two leaders would talk again in the coming weeks in the presence of outgoing UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

“We are continuing this effort with absolute seriousness and one single goal: resuming the talks before the ‌end ‌of the secretary-general’s term,” at the end of the year, Christodoulides told reporters after the meeting.

Guterres began a new drive to try to resolve the more than five-decade-old conflict in the summer, suggesting new crossings could build trust and confidence. However, the two sides have since been disagreeing ‌over the ground rules for talks.

The move would bring the number of open crossings on the divided Mediterranean island to 11, according ⁠to media in Cyprus.

Cyprus was split in 1974 when Turkiye invaded and seized the northern part in response to a coup instigated by the then-military government in Greece.

A previous power-sharing administration of Greek and Turkish Cypriots had fallen apart in 1963, and a UN Peacekeeping Force has monitored a 180km (112-mile) ceasefire line which splits the two sides since.

Only Turkiye recognises the northern part of the island as an independent republic. Ankara maintains more than 35,000 troops on Cyprus.

Decades of talks have repeatedly failed to reunify Cyprus, with the last official round collapsing in 2017. Greek Cypriots are against Ankara having any hands-on involvement; Turkish Cypriots say it is essential.

Last year, the north elected its first pro-unification leader since 2020, generating renewed hope.

articles.title: New California law will restrict sales of some muscle-building supplements to minors
articles.excerpt:
Fox News medical contributor Dr. Jessica Gray discusses research connecting energy drinks and workout supplements to increased heart problems.

Gavin Newsom has signed legislation banning the sale of ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News medical contributor Dr. Jessica Gray discusses research connecting energy drinks and workout supplements to increased heart problems.

Gavin Newsom has signed legislation banning the sale of some "muscle-building supplements" to Californians under 18 years of age.

The legislation (AB 2030), which was signed on Sept. 28, covers over-the-counter diet pills and dietary supplements for weight loss or muscle building. It will go into effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

"Nonprescribed, medically unapproved products may cause dangerous side effects," the governor’s office said in its announcement. "Products can be mislabeled or contaminated with substances such as steroids."

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

California’s law restricts minors’ access to supplements marketed for muscle building – specifically, those that are "labeled, marketed or otherwise represented for the purpose of achieving weight loss or building muscle."

New California legislation will ban the sale of some "muscle-building supplements" to Californians under 18 years of age. (iStock)

Courts may consider whether a product contains "creatine, green tea extract, raspberry ketone, garcinia cambogia or green coffee bean extract," the legislation states.

The law does not impose an outright ban on all creatine products. Restrictions depend on how the supplements are labeled, advertised and marketed to consumers.

TAKING DAILY SUPPLEMENT MAY HELP PRESERVE MUSCLE AS YOU AGE — EVEN WITHOUT EXERCISE

The law does not apply to people under 18 who have a prescription for an over-the-counter diet pill or dietary supplement for weight loss or muscle-building.

The release cites research indicating that nearly one in 10 adolescents have used such products.

The legislation (AB 2030), which was signed on Sept. 28, covers over-the-counter diet pills and dietary supplements for weight loss or muscle building. (iStock)

It also references studies linking over-the-counter diet pill use to a sixfold greater likelihood of an eating disorder diagnosis within three years.

The announcement does not specify whether whey protein or creatine products are included in the ban.

Sellers who do not adhere to the new law will face civil fines of up to $500 per violation.

"Nonprescribed, medically unapproved products may cause dangerous side effects."

The American Herbal Products Association, based in Maryland, released a statement opposing the law.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Lacking any scientific justification, AB 2030 casts a shadow over safe, beneficial products," said Robert Marriott, the association's vice president of regulatory and government affairs, in the statement.

The organization argues that the law's scope is unclear and notes that it does not explicitly exempt protein products.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Center for Science in the Public Interest, based in Washington, D.C., shared public support of the new legislation.

POPULAR DRINKS LINKED TO HEART ATTACKS, CARDIAC ARREST IN YOUNG ADULTS, STUDY FINDS

"Manufacturers of these products often prey on kids and teens with deceptive claims that lack any scientific evidence," said Jensen Jose, a regulatory counsel at CSPI, which co-sponsored the legislation.

"Studies show that many supplements contain harmful substances that go undetected," one physician warned. (iStock)

Dr. Sigrid Wolf, a pediatric sports medicine physician at Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago, recently addressed the use of creatine products among teenagers, stating that evidence of benefits is limited.

POISON CENTERS LINK GROWING BENADRYL ABUSE AMONG TEENS TO DANGEROUS SOCIAL MEDIA TRENDS

"In some cases, they might even be dangerous," wrote Wolf, who is a member of the American Academy of Pediatrics' sports medicine committee, in an article published on HealthyChildren.org, the American Academy of Pediatrics' parenting website.

"Creatine can come with negative side effects such as weight gain, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea."

"Studies show that many supplements contain harmful substances that go undetected," she added, instead recommending prioritizing nutrition, training, sleep and hydration.

Fox News Digital reached out to Newsom's office for comment.

Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

articles.title: Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy to be retried on murder charges
articles.excerpt:
Massachusetts judge rejects bid by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed

A Massachusetts judge cleared the way on Monday for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on ⁠murder charges fo...
articles.body_text:
Massachusetts judge rejects bid by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed

A Massachusetts judge cleared the way on Monday for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on ⁠murder charges for killing her three young children at her home in 2023, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject her to a ⁠double prosecution for the same ⁠crime.

Judge William ​Sullivan in Plymouth rejected a bid by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed. The judge on 4 September declared ⁠a mistrial after the jury reported that a holdout juror was preventing it from reaching a unanimous verdict.

The judge has scheduled a 16 November hearing to ⁠discuss when to hold a second trial, which he has suggested could occur in March.

No one ​at Clancy’s initial trial disputed that ‌she strangled daughter Cora, five; son ‌Dawson, three; and eight-month-old son Callan with exercise bands on 24 January 2023, in the ‌basement of their home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury.

She then cut herself with a knife and jumped from a second-story window in an attempt to end her own life, leaving her paralyzed.

Her lawyers have argued Clancy was in the throes of postpartum psychosis and should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of ‌criminal responsibility.

Some of the jurors in televised interviews later said that, but for one holdout juror, they had been prepared to find Clancy not guilty by ​reason of insanity. Such a verdict would have resulted in her commitment to a state psychiatric hospital, subject to regular court review.

In Massachusetts, a conviction on first-degree murder charges carries a mandatory sentence of life in prison without parole.

Defense lawyers argued that a retrial would violate Clancy’s constitutional protection against ⁠being tried twice for the same crime, known as double jeopardy, saying ​Sullivan acted prematurely in declaring a ​mistrial and should have pursued ​a viable alternative.

Citing jury notes that stated the holdout juror was not following ​the law on reasonable ‌doubt despite the ​judge’s instructions, defense lawyers ​said Sullivan should have instead questioned the holdout and potentially removed the juror.

Prosecutors under Plymouth county district attorney Timothy Cruz countered that the judge handled the jury impasse appropriately and that questioning the holdout could have risked the judge inappropriately interfering with jury deliberations.

articles.title: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
articles.excerpt:
A fire broke out at the factory following the explosion which some eyewitnesses confused with an earthquake

At least 17 people have died and 12 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and...
articles.body_text:
A fire broke out at the factory following the explosion which some eyewitnesses confused with an earthquake

At least 17 people have died and 12 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey.

All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said. Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air.

The local governor said the blast happened around midday after a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below.

Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, the Turkish Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent civil society organisation, said.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan originally said the death toll was 16, but later Health Minister Kemal Memişoğlu announced that one of those who had been critically injured had later died of their injuries, taking the toll to 17.

Eyewitnesses at the scene of the incident said the explosion shook the ground, with one person initially believing an earthquake had struck.

In a statement, the company that runs the factory said the accident occurred during scheduled maintenance work on one of the plant's electric arc furnaces.

Izmir Governor Süleyman Elban told media that some people were believed to still be under the rubble.

Speaking after a cabinet meeting on Monday, Erdoğan confirmed the deaths and said investigations were under way, while search and rescue operations continued.

At least five people have been arrested, according BBC News's Turkish service, citing local media reports.

The Habas plant is in the Izmir district of Aliaga which is a major port and one of Turkey's main shipbreaking hubs.

articles.title: Jared Goff's SI Swimsuit wife had a big Miami weekend, college football gets greedy & Christmas decor time?
articles.excerpt:

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up o...
articles.body_text:
The selection committee has officially traded credibility for drama, ranking manufactured television narratives instead of actual on-field resumes.

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

My wife pulled the rug out from under me and ripped down all the Halloween decor around the house over the weekend. Didn't even give me warning. No heads-up. I left Friday morning and everything was pumpkins and cobwebs, and by the time I got home late in the afternoon, it may as well have been May.

What a punch to the gut. I went to Target later that day, and it was pretty much Santa's workshop in there. Christmas music blaring down every aisle. Reindeer hanging from the ceilings. Ribbons everywhere.

And just like that, fall was over — and the holiday season had begun. I held out for as long as I could, but I was ambushed. Now, we're in an undecorated house because the Christmas stuff is in the attic and, frankly, I don't have it in me to go up there quite yet.

So, we wait. Perhaps this weekend, when a cold front is supposed to be in town for a few days? An actual cold front. Our first since March!

Until then, we're in November purgatory. Sad.

NFL WEEK 9 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS, 49ERS AND PACKERS LOOK SUPER, RAMS FINALLY OVER .500

Christen Harper attends the 2023 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue Launch at Hard Rock Hotel New York on May 18, 2023, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Jared Goff's wife, Christen Harper, had a dominant weekend in Miami and helped the Lions to a 19-9 win over my Miami Dolphins.

Most ethical tank ever, though. What a pleasure it's been to watch this season!

What else? I've got college football officially killing off conference championship weekend, Ron DeSantis (sadly, the outgoing governor of the great state of Florida) weighs in like the PATRIOT he is, and when is an acceptable time to put the Christmas decorations up?

You all know where I stand, but I'm curious to see if I'm in the majority or minority here.

OK, grab you something to deck your halls (whatever that means), and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

Big college football Saturday, and a big NFL Sunday yesterday. Let's spin the wheel and start the week with ...

The NFL! We'll get to college here in a bit. Crooks.

Pretty solid Sunday of football, right? Browns-Saints was a good one. Cowboys-Colts was a mess. The Pats got absolutely steamrolled, which was nice to watch as a Dolphins fan.

And my Dolphins ... continued the most ethical tank in NFL history yesterday against the Lions. I've watched a lot of tanks in my 30 years as a Fins fan, and what the fellas are doing this season is a true masterpiece.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S COWBOY HAT MESSAGE HAS FANS TALKING, HOLLY ROWE'S WNBA FINALS PLAN & IS TEXAS' FIELD GRAY?

The defense — truly a no-name defense — held the best offense in football to 19 points yesterday. Nineteen! Quick, name ONE person on the Miami defense.

You can't. I barely can, and I watch the games!

I was a little skeptical coming into this season about how I'd feel week in and week out rooting for a team that just stinks. I've gotta say — it's been a pleasure. Seriously.

There is absolutely no pressure on NFL Sundays anymore. None. The team is young, playing well, and losing every game because they just don't have the talent. It's a win-win. I miss watching a winning team, and I miss the feeling of winning a big game. Winning on NFL Sunday is the absolute best feeling as a sports fan.

But boy, it's been nice to be stress-free, too.

Now, let's check in with Jared Goff's SI Swimsuit wife, Christen Goff (Harper), and get this week started right:

Christen Goff attends the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Runway Show during Swim Week at W South Beach in Miami Beach, Fla., on May 30, 2026. (Alexander Tamargo/Getty Images for Sports Illustrated)

Indeed, Christen. You did. Can't argue that. Get us now, NFL, while you still can. The Dolphins are COMING.

PS: Shoutout to Jahmyr Gibbs for scoring the game's only touchdown yesterday. I had Gibbs, Ken Walker and George Pickens parlayed for all three to score the first touchdown in their respective games. Walker hit early. Gibbs finally hit in the third quarter (!!!). Pickens never played!

Not a bad little payout, which I needed because I got absolutely slaughtered by the books on Saturday.

Speaking of college football ... it's official, folks. The playoff will expand to 24 teams next season, and conference title games will be officially eliminated.

"A short-sighted move that might bolster profits in the near term but will further erode what has traditionally made college football special," DeSantis posted in response to Monday's official announcement.

I've said from the beginning that I don't love any of it. Now, I do love more playoff games on actual campuses. That's the biggest issue I have with the current format. Neutral site games are for the birds when it comes to college football. Every single game should be on a college campus. I'll die on that hill.

But the elimination of Championship Weekend hurts. I hate it. The first Friday and Saturday of December are unofficial holidays, as far as I'm concerned. Back in the day you'd have the Pac-12 title game on Friday, and the Big 12, SEC, ACC and Big Ten on Saturday — in that order.

Georgia head coach Kirby Smart and team celebrate after winning the Southeastern Conference Championship Game against Alabama on Dec. 6, 2025, in Atlanta, Georgia. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

It was awesome. We have one more dance with it next month, and then it's gone forever.

Soak it all in, folks. You will miss it this time next year. I promise.

Speaking of missing things, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night of FOOTBALL.

First up? This came across my desk today, and I've watched it 50 times already:

Today is the 24-year anniversary of LSU's improbable Hail Mary against Kentucky, better known as the Bluegrass Miracle.

More importantly ... it was played on Jefferson-Pilot Sports, which is pure nostalgia for kids my age that grew up in the south.

Remember Jefferson-Pilot? Man, was it the best.

Nothing – and I mean nothing – beat going from College GameDay to whatever third-tier SEC game Jefferson-Pilot was airing at noon. Jay Cutler and Eli Manning had some EPIC showdowns on JP back in the day. It was never the best game, or the best picture quality, or the best announcers.

But buddy, it was college football at it's best. That's what they're taking from us!

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. I leave you with Sophie Cunningham at yesterday's NASCAR finale in Homestead, and a question:

When do YOU put up the Christmas decorations? It's been nine days since Halloween. Too early? Too late? What's the cutoff?

articles.title: Chris Rock says he 'was not a great husband' to Malaak Compton-Rock, admits he watched 'a lot of porn'
articles.excerpt:
Comedian Chris Rock compared the institutionalization of woke culture to the Salem witch trials, sparking criticism from 'The Five' for addressing the issue several years 'late.'

Chris Rock is going ...
articles.body_text:
Comedian Chris Rock compared the institutionalization of woke culture to the Salem witch trials, sparking criticism from 'The Five' for addressing the issue several years 'late.'

Chris Rock is going into detail about the end of his marriage, admitting he wasn't the best husband and took accountability for mistakes he made in the relationship.

During a recent interview with GQ, the 61-year-old comedian shared that there were many factors that caused the divorce, noting he cheated and was addicted to pornography during his marriage.

"I was not a great husband," he admitted. "I watched a lot of porn. I don’t watch porn anymore. I haven’t watched porn in five, six years."

He also admitted to cheating on his wife, noting, "It’s not anything I’m proud of, but it’s something I had to go through."

Rock took ownership of the fact that he cheated on his wife and was addicted to pornography. (Richard Burbridge/GQ)

CHRIS ROCK SHREDS 'WOKE 1.0' ERA, COMPARES MODERN OUTRAGE TO SALEM WITCH HUNTS

The comedian compared himself to a character in a Marvel movie who "has to test his powers" and see how far they can push things before they eventually "crash down."

"Every Marvel movie, man or woman, they have to test their powers," he said. "They’re a- -holes. They get these powers and they’re a- -holes, and they’re racing trains and they’re lifting up ocean liners and they try to go to the sun, then they crash down because they realize they’re not God. And then they start helping people."

Rock compared himself to a superhero learning he had powers and pushing the limits. (Simon Ackerman/Getty Images for BFI)

He explained that he "tested my powers" during his marriage by cheating on his wife, noting he "was severely humbled" when he realized he definitely "wasn't God or anywhere near him."

Rock was married to Malaak Compton-Rock for nearly 20 years. They tied the knot in 1996, separated in 2014 and finalized their divorce in 2016. They share two children together, daughters, Lola and Zahra.

The comedian was married to Malaak Compton-Rock for nearly 20 years before separating in 2014. (Kris Connor/Getty Images)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The actor recently directed the film, "Misty Green," the first movie he has directed in 12 years, the last one being 2014's "Top Five." He explained that some of the reason behind that is that he got divorced.

Rock recently directed the film, "Misty Green." (Richard Burbridge/GQ)

"Nobody has a successful divorce, so that takes time," he said. "Then once it’s done, okay, you’re not sitting on the money you had before, so now you got to really make some money. So you go on tour, or two tours. So there was a lot of stand-up. There was a lot of getting my life together. You got a pandemic, you got a bunch of nonsense going on there."

"Misty Green" is the first film Rock has directed in 12 years. (Rosalind O'Connor/NBC via Getty Images)

"Misty Green" follows an award-winning actress, Misty Green, who is working hard to make a comeback after years of watching her career slowly fade away, with Rock portraying a casting director who once worked with the actress.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

While promoting the movie, Rock told "The Daily" podcast in October that he wanted to make a movie about Los Angeles, calling it a "tale of two cities," noting that while there is "sunshine and palm trees," people are also "constantly walking over homeless people."

Chris Rock said L.A. attracts a dark "underbelly" which he wanted to show in his new film. (Getty Images for Night of Too Many Stars)

The actor previously spoke about the message he wanted to get across when making the film, telling Variety in September that much of the movie is about Los Angeles, which he called a "complicated place" that "attracts an underbelly that people want to pretend doesn’t exist."

"A lot of it’s about L.A. L.A. has got very wonky priorities," he said. "There’s a real estate office on the same street as The Ivy on Robertson, and in the window, there are houses for $30-$40 million. In the window. But there’s a homeless guy sleeping right outside. The movie is about that crazy dichotomy."

Rock wanted to make a film about Los Angeles. (Richard Burbridge/GQ)

articles.title: WWE legend shares the importance of standing for the national anthem, working with US military members

In a world where standing for...
articles.body_text:
The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries walking off the court for the national anthem doesn't sit well with John Rocker, calling the situation "utterly disgusting."

In a world where standing for the national anthem with your hand over your heart has become a topic for debate, WWE Hall of Famer Goldberg left no doubt on where he stood on the issue.

Goldberg, whose real name is Bill Goldberg, appeared on NewsNation and told former Charlotte 49ers head football coach Bill Poggi that his respect, appreciation and admiration for those who have served in the U.S. military is the reason why he shows allegiance when "The Star-Spangled Banner" is played.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Goldberg enters the ring during Saturday Night's Main Event at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Ga., on July 12, 2025. (WWE via Getty Images)

"Well, especially in today's day and age when people like to forget history and people don't necessarily appreciate who came before them," he said. "I stand for the national anthem and I put my hand over my heart because there's so many people who have put their lives on the line for people that they don't know just as a job to protect the country. And that, in itself, is a reason to stand up and show allegiance. I cannot tell you the joy that I get out of seeing these men and women deployed and deriving some type of enjoyment and excitement to interact with someone such as myself. So why wouldn't you spread that as much as humanly possible and make it part of every day of your life to try to put a smile on somebody's face and, in this case, a veteran who again put their lives on the line for people that they don't even know to serve their country?

"So for me, if I can go out of my way to pat someone on the back and look them in the eye and say thank you and have them understand that it's truly coming from my heart with no ulterior motive whatsoever. I don't care about getting somebody taking a picture of me shaking somebody's hand and posting it and showing what a good guy I am. That's not why I do it. I do it because I can look in their eye and see how much they appreciate it."

Goldberg credited his parents, his sister and those who came before him with teaching him "how to be a human being." He said, now, taking care of his children and his family along with "taking care of our military" are some of the most important things in his life.

WWE Hall of Fame member Bill Goldberg practices for the 58th annual Food City 500 on Saturday, April 14, 2018, at Bristol Motor Speedway in Bristol, Tenn. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

CARTON RIPS INTO PHILADELPHIA EAGLES HEAD COACH NICK SIRIANNI, SAYS HE COACHED HIS EVER GAME IN PHILADELPHIA - LISTEN NOW

He called it a "duty" to put a smile on somebody’s face whether it’s because they know him from his NFL, pro wrestling or acting backgrounds.

"And so I will service the kids and the military till the day I die," he added. "And it means everything to me. It truly does."

Goldberg played 14 games in the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons between 1992 and 1994. He also spent time in the World League of American Football. After being cut by the Carolina Panthers in 1995, he would pop up in World Championship Wrestling (WCW) by the end of 1997.

Nose guard Bill Goldberg Jr. of the University of Georgia Bulldogs is on the field during a game against the Florida Gators on Nov. 5, 1988, at The Swamp in Gainesville, Fla. Georgia won 26-3. (Getty Images)

He won the WCW World Heavyweight Championship once and was a three-time world champion in WWE.

The WWE inducted him into its Hall of Fame in 2018.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.excerpt:
Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month

France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised th...
articles.body_text:
Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month

France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.

Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.

Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen anc chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.

Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".

He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".

France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.

The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.

Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.

Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.

In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.

If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy.

On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.

More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.

Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.

The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.

Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.

Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.

In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.

The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.

Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack

UK meat industry hit by cyber-attack which targeted European supermarket freezers

If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?
